M0 invisibility proof — compositor and seam
docs/plans/active/workspace-windowing-system.md, M0 ship criterion

M0 changes how the workspace preview is composed, not what it draws: the box
type, the frame's ownership of a leaf's header row, the canvas blit that
replaced the two-leaf joins, the content contract, one zoom rule, hit regions
registered from the placements the canvas drew from, and one floors authority.
The claim the milestone makes is that none of it reaches a cell, with one
deliberate exception recorded under "The one thing that moved" below.

This directory is the part of that claim a real Sidecar process can be driven
through. It reaches the one-leaf pane tree only. The composition M0 actually
rewrote — a document pane beside the terminal — cannot be reached headlessly and
is measured in Go instead; both halves are named here rather than one standing
in for the other.

Method
------
Two binaries, one built at db8c342 (the tree M0 started from) and one at the
head of M0, driven through the same key sequence at two sizes, on private tmux
servers and private state trees. The captures below are the M0 binary's
ANSI-stripped pane text with trailing spaces removed; the comparison itself was
made on the raw captures, escape sequences included, so a styling change would
have shown even where the glyphs agreed.

Every state below matched byte for byte at both sizes. The only masked
difference is the header and footer clock, which advances between two runs by
construction. No transcript in this repository was re-recorded, because none of
them holds a state whose cells M0 moved.

Isolation (`./scripts/tmux-drive.sh paths` before each run)
  outer server  -L sidecar-drive
  base run dir  /private/tmp/sidecar-m0-base-501
  head run dir  /private/tmp/sidecar-m0-head-501
  inner tmux    <run dir>/tmux/tmux-501/default
  state home    <run dir>/state
  config        <run dir>/config/config.json
  SIDECAR_ISOLATED_STATE=1
The machine's default tmux server was never started, stopped, or sent a command.

Reproduce
---------
  mkdir -p /tmp/sidecar-m0-base-src
  git archive db8c342 | tar -x -C /tmp/sidecar-m0-base-src
  (cd /tmp/sidecar-m0-base-src && go build -o sidecar-base ./cmd/sidecar)
  go build -o /tmp/sidecar-m0-head/sidecar ./cmd/sidecar

  # once per binary, with SIDECAR_DRIVE_RUN_DIR and SIDECAR_BIN set to it:
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh start 200 50     -> wide-01-startup
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh keys 4           -> wide-02-workspaces
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh keys j           -> wide-03-after-j
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh keys j           -> wide-04-after-jj
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh keys 2           -> wide-05-git
  ./scripts/tmux-drive.sh stop
  # then the same sequence at 100x30 for the narrow-* captures

  diff <(sed 's/[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]/CLOCK/g' base/<state>.txt) \
       <(sed 's/[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]/CLOCK/g' head/<state>.txt)

What each state exercises
-------------------------
  01-startup      App chrome and the td plugin: the frame M0 did not touch,
                  present so a difference anywhere would be attributable.
  02-workspaces   The workspace sidebar beside the preview box. The preview is
                  the terminal leaf of a one-leaf pane tree, so this is the
                  path where terminalLeafBox now reads Zoomed and the floors
                  from one authority instead of its own literal.
  03-after-j      Selection moves to a shell; the preview follows it. The
                  terminal surface is composed from the leaf box.
  04-after-jj     Selection on a workspace with no agent: the same leaf box
                  with a different content.
  05-git          Leaving the plugin, to catch a change that only shows once
                  the workspace view has been built and torn down.

What this cannot reach, and where that half is measured
-------------------------------------------------------
A doc leaf is born from a markdown path in live agent output, so no key sequence
puts a document beside the terminal. Two Go tests carry that half of the claim:

  TestTwoLeafPaneCompositionMatchesTheJoinsItReplaced
  (internal/plugins/workspace/pane_composition_parity_test.go) reproduces the
  deleted lipgloss joins over the same leaf blocks the canvas composes and holds
  the two to the same string, across both axes, both child orders, both focus
  states, four sizes and six preview content states — 192 configurations, the
  shape the product ships.

  The cell-exact goldens over a three-leaf, a nested four-leaf and a
  three-deep five-leaf tree in
  internal/plugins/workspace/pane_compositor_test.go assert every composed cell,
  each divider's own box, and every leaf and divider hit region, for trees the
  two-leaf renderer could not compose at all.

The one thing that moved
------------------------
The canvas holds every leaf to the rectangle the layout gave it. The joins
placed the divider at the widest line — or the last row — of the block beside
it, because that is what lipgloss joins do. So wherever the terminal leaf
rendered short of its box (no agent attached, an orphaned worktree, the welcome
guide, the Diff and Task tabs, or output simply narrower than the pane), the
pre-M0 divider and the document beside it hugged that content instead of
standing where the split put them.

Measured over the parity test's own 192 configurations with the leaf renderers
restored to their pre-M0 shape: 148 of 192 disagree, on both axes. As shipped:
0 of 192. One example, 140x36, a workspace with no agent, a 50/50 column split —
the divider stood at column 24 and now stands at column 70, which is where the
ratio puts it.

This is the one place M0 changes what a user sees, and the change is from a
divider placed by the length of a line to a divider placed by the layout. None
of the captures in this directory holds a document pane, which is why none of
them was re-recorded.
